comment: The built-in functions DuckDB 2.0's binder folds into constants when they are stable within a query (probed on v2.0.0-alpha48256 by `SELECT year(current_date)`-style plans with the optimizer off: the call is gone from the plan and a constant of the day of lowering stands in its place, also inside date_trunc, age, +, -, date_diff, timezone, epoch_ms ...). The planning connections register a volatile function of the same name and type over each, so the plan keeps the call. Docs: docs/research/duckdb-2.0/README.md, section 2026-10-15 (the override). `value` says how the replacement computes what the built-in would: the time kinds read the clock when the function runs (DuckDB's TimeZone setting of the connection when it was registered; the planning connections never change it), `captured` kinds are what the same connection answered to `capture` just before the registration (the planning connections are fresh, in-memory, and never change schema, database or transaction).

notCovered.name: current_schemas
notCovered.reason: returns VARCHAR[]; a list vector is not written by the override, so a call still folds to a constant list on 2.0 (the lowerer refuses nested values)

notCovered.name: current_setting
notCovered.reason: its result type is the setting's own (ANY), which a registered function cannot reproduce; a call folds to a constant of the setting's value

notCovered.name: getvariable
notCovered.reason: ANY result like current_setting; a variable is a connection value that the binder reads as a constant on every version

notCovered.name: getenv
notCovered.reason: folds to the environment of the machine that plans; the tool never lowers it for an engine (it has no equivalent)
